heard: Tiny dwarf galaxies are leaking oxygen into deep space. Every breath we take was forged inside a star. When stars explode as supernovae, they expel that oxygen. Most massive galaxies have enough gravity to trap it, but NASA's Hubble found these tiny star systems are empty. Violent galactic winds act like a massive cosmic purge. These gales blast oxygen entirely out of the galaxy's reach. These tiny systems are the universe's primary chemical polluters. That's why tiny dwarf galaxies are leaking oxygen into deep space.
